hooks.text: Cutting a jammed solar panel flung two astronauts into space.
What catapulted two spacewalking astronauts directly into space?
A simple metal strap nearly destroyed America's first space station.

title: The Spacewalk Repair That Catapulted Astronauts
description: During an emergency repair on Skylab in 1973, freeing a jammed solar wing flung two astronauts into space.

beats.text: Cutting a jammed solar panel flung two astronauts into space.
queries: Pete Conrad solar array EVA Skylab

beats.text: Launch forces had ripped away Skylab's shield and main solar panel.
beats.visual: Skylab space station in orbit showing launch damage, 1973

beats.text: Internal station heat quickly climbed past 130 degrees Fahrenheit.
beats.visual: Diagram illustrating the internal layout of Skylab space station, 1973

beats.text: The crew first pushed a replacement parasol out to cool it down.
beats.visual: Emergency parasol thermal sunshade deployed on Skylab, 1973

beats.text: Next, astronauts Charles Conrad and Joseph Kerwin used a 25-foot pole cutter.
queries: Charles Conrad Paul Weitz Joseph Kerwin

beats.text: The trapped solar wing suddenly snapped open under massive tension.
beats.visual: Spacewalk repair to free the jammed solar array beam on Skylab, 1973
queries: Pete Conrad solar array EVA Skylab

beats.text: Thin safety tethers were all that kept them from drifting away.
beats.visual: Astronauts training for the solar array repair underwater, 1973
queries: Marshall Space Flight Center underwater suit training

beats.text: Power returned, saving the station after their dangerous recoil.
beats.visual: Apollo Command Module docked to Skylab station in orbit, 1973

better_than_last: Applied seamless circular looping back to the opening hook while introducing the escalating mechanical emergency directly in the early beats.
